# Opposite-hole split does not force edge-order amalgamation

## Composition

(none yet)

## Development

In the twelve-label opposite-hole split residue, each relevant non-Hamiltonian five-set is edge-orderable, but the two edge orders on one side need not amalgamate over their shared Hamiltonian four-set. A SAT witness exists in which the union comparison digraph contains the directed star triangle ab -> bq_2 -> by -> ab, equivalently h(a,b,q_2)=h(q_2,b,y)=h(y,b,a)=1. Each individual bad K5 comparison digraph remains acyclic. Thus the acyclic amalgamation seen in one canonical survivor is not forced. The correct dichotomy is: either the two side orders amalgamate, or their first incompatibility can already occur as a bounded cross-side comparison cycle; a star triangle is feasible. Any proof using a mostly ordered six-shadow in this opposite-hole regime must therefore handle such comparison-cycle certificates explicitly.
